description: After identifying field boundaries via SIMD, materialize parsed output in columnar (column-major) format rather than row-major, writing each field to its corresponding column buffer. This converts the row-oriented scatter pattern into sequential column writes, dramatically improving cache utilization for downstream analytics (which typically process one column at a time). Directly produces Apache Arrow-compatible columnar batches.
mathematical_formalization: For a CSV with C columns and R rows in a batch: Row-major materialization generates C*R random writes. Columnar materialization generates C sequential write streams. Cache miss model: row-major = O(C * R / L) misses (L = cache line size) when C > cache ways; columnar = O(R * C / L) with spatial locality. For C > cache associativity, columnar is O(C/assoc) times fewer misses.
analogical_connections: Array-of-Structures vs Structure-of-Arrays (AoS vs SoA): classic game engine optimization where SoA layout enables SIMD vectorization of physics/rendering
Matrix transposition: the row-to-column conversion is a streaming transpose, amenable to cache-oblivious or tiled algorithms
ETL pipeline design: the 'extract-then-pivot' pattern mirrors data warehouse loading strategies
implementation_hypothesis: Allocate C column buffers (one per CSV column). During field extraction, maintain C write cursors. For each row, write field[j] to column_buffer[j][write_cursor[j]++]. Use batch sizes aligned to cache line boundaries (e.g., 1024 rows). For variable-length string columns, use an offsets array + contiguous data buffer (Arrow StringArray layout). For numeric columns, parse-and-convert inline to avoid double-materialization.
experiment_seed: Compare columnar vs. row-major materialization on a 1GB CSV with 20 columns. Measure: (1) L1/L2/L3 cache miss rates via perf counters, (2) total parsing+materialization throughput, (3) downstream query speed (sum of one numeric column). Use Intel VTune or perf stat.
